section.title: Chapter review and discovery problems
section.p: This chapter began with one small calculation: \frac{(2+h)^2-2^2}{h}=4+h for h\neq 0. The forbidden value h=0 did not stop us from discovering the behavior near 0. That central intuition grew into limits, continuity, asymptotes, sequences, and fundamental existence theorems.

figure.caption: Limits are the center. Continuity, asymptotes, sequences, and tangent slopes all use the same idea of controlled approach.

subsection.title: A decision guide for limits and continuity

table.title: Problem-solving strategies for limits and continuity

row.cell: Direct substitution gives a real number
Use continuity or algebraic limit laws directly.
Factor, cancel, rationalize, or expand; then substitute again.
Left and right sides behave differently
Compute one-sided limits \lim_{x\to a^-} and \lim_{x\to a^+}.
Check signs on both sides for infinite limits (\pm\infty).
Divide numerator and denominator by highest power of x.
Bounded oscillation multiplied by something small
Verify continuity, closed interval, and boundedness hypotheses.
Use \varepsilon-N definitions or Monotone Convergence Theorem.

statement.p: Explain the difference between \lim_{x\to a}f(x) and f(a). Give an example where the limit exists but does not equal the function value.
Explain why the condition 0\lt |x-a|\lt \delta appears in the definition of a limit.
What does the statement \lim_{x\to a}f(x)=\infty mean? Why is this not convergence to a real number?
A table gives values of f(x) near x=3 approaching 8. Why is the table useful, but not a proof?
State the two-sided limit test using left-hand and right-hand limits.
In your own words, explain what continuity at a means.
Why can a removable discontinuity be repaired by redefining one single point, while a jump discontinuity cannot?
State the Intermediate Value Theorem and identify its main hypothesis.
State the Extreme Value Theorem. Explain why both closed and bounded are essential hypotheses.
Explain the difference between convergence of a sequence and convergence of a series using the terms terms and partial sums.

exercisegroup.title: B. Skills: compute and interpret limits

statement.p: Compute: (a) \lim_{x\to 3}\frac{x^2-9}{x-3}, (b) \lim_{x\to 2}\frac{x^3-8}{x-2}, (c) \lim_{x\to 4}\frac{\sqrt{x+5}-3}{x-4}, (d) \lim_{x\to 2}\frac{\frac{1}{x}-\frac{1}{2}}{x-2}.
Use the Squeeze Theorem to evaluate: (a) \lim_{x\to 0}x\sin(1/x), (b) \lim_{x\to 0}x^2\cos(1/x^2), (c) \lim_{x\to 0}|x|\sin(1/x).
Let F(x)=\begin{cases}x^2+2, \amp x\lt 1 \\ 4, \amp x=1 \\ 3x, \amp x\gt 1\end{cases}. Find \lim_{x\to 1^-}F(x), \lim_{x\to 1^+}F(x), \lim_{x\to 1}F(x), and F(1). Is F continuous at 1?
Let G(x)=\begin{cases}2x+1, \amp x\lt 2 \\ 5, \amp x=2 \\ x^2-1, \amp x\gt 2\end{cases}. Find left, right, two-sided limits and G(2). Classify the discontinuity.
Evaluate: (a) \lim_{x\to 3^-}\frac{1}{x-3}, (b) \lim_{x\to 3^+}\frac{1}{x-3}, (c) \lim_{x\to 3}\frac{1}{(x-3)^2}, (d) \lim_{x\to 2^-}\frac{x+2}{x^2-4}, (e) \lim_{x\to 2^+}\frac{x+2}{x^2-4}.
Evaluate: (a) \lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{5x^2-x+1}{2x^2+3}, (b) \lim_{x\to -\infty}\frac{5x^2-x+1}{2x^2+3}, (c) \lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{3x+7}{x^2+1}, (d) \lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{x^2+1}{x-1}.
Write \frac{x^2+3x}{x+1} in the form mx+b+\frac{r}{x+1} and identify slant asymptotes as x\to\pm\infty.
Find sequence limits: (a) \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{3n+1}{2n-5}, (b) \lim_{n\to\infty}(1-1/n), (c) \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{n^2+4}{5n^2-n}, (d) \lim_{n\to\infty}(-1)^n.
Classify monotonicity, boundedness, and convergence for: (a) a_n=1-1/n, (b) b_n=1/n, (c) c_n=n, (d) d_n=(-1)^n.

exercisegroup.title: C. Reading limits from a graph

figure.caption: Graph for reading one-sided limits, function values, and discontinuities.

statement.p: Find \lim_{x\to -1^-}f(x), \lim_{x\to -1^+}f(x), \lim_{x\to -1}f(x), and f(-1).
Find \lim_{x\to 1^-}f(x), \lim_{x\to 1^+}f(x), \lim_{x\to 1}f(x), and f(1).
Identify all points of discontinuity and classify each as removable or jump.
Could changing only f(-1) make the function continuous at -1?
Could changing only f(1) make the function continuous at 1?
Find c making H(x)=\begin{cases}x^2+c, \amp x\lt 2 \\ 3x-1, \amp x\ge 2\end{cases} continuous at x=2.
Find c making K(x)=\begin{cases}\frac{x^2-4}{x-2}, \amp x\neq 2 \\ c, \amp x=2\end{cases} continuous at x=2.
Find all discontinuities of R(x)=\frac{x+1}{x^2-1} and classify them as removable or infinite.
Use IVT to prove x^3+x-3=0 has a solution in (1,2).
Use IVT to prove x^5+x-1=0 has a solution in (0,1).
Explain why f(x)=x^4-4x+1 attains an absolute maximum and minimum on [-2,3].
Does EVT guarantee extrema for f(x)=1/x on (0,1)? Which hypothesis fails?
If f is continuous on [0,4] with f(0)=-2 and f(4)=7, what values must f take?
If g is not continuous on [0,4] with g(0)=-2 and g(4)=7, must g(c)=0 for some c?
Give an example of a continuous function on an unbounded interval with no absolute maximum.

exercisegroup.title: E. Proof practice with \varepsilon, \delta, and N

statement.p: Prove from definition that \lim_{x\to 3}(2x+5)=11.
Prove from definition that \lim_{x\to a}(mx+b)=ma+b.
Prove from definition that \lim_{x\to 2}x^2=4.
Prove from definition that \lim_{x\to 1}\frac{x^2-1}{x-1}=2.
Prove that \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}=0 using the precise sequence definition.
Prove that \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{2n+1}{n+3}=2.
Prove directly that a_n=1-1/n \to 1.
Show that b_n=(-1)^n diverges.
For \varepsilon=10^{-4}, find N such that n\ge N \implies |1/n - 0|\lt 10^{-4}.
For a_n=\frac{n}{n+1}, find N such that n\ge N \implies |a_n-1|\lt 0.001.

subsection.title: Project: bisection method for a root
subsection.p: The Intermediate Value Theorem proves roots exist; bisection turns that proof into a reliable numerical method for p(x)=x^3-x-1=0 on [1,2].
After N iterations, the error satisfies |M_N-c|\le \frac{R_0-L_0}{2^{N+1}} = \frac{1}{2^{N+1}}.

subsection.title: Discovery problems: secant slopes becoming tangent slopes
subsection.p: For a function f, point a, and increment h\neq 0, the secant slope is \frac{f(a+h)-f(a)}{h}. The derivative is defined by the limit as h\to 0.

statement.p: For f(x)=x^2 at a=2, let m_n = \frac{f(2+1/n)-f(2)}{1/n} = 4+\frac{1}{n}. As n\to\infty, m_n \to 4.
From the left, \ell_n = \frac{f(2-1/n)-f(2)}{-1/n} = 4-\frac{1}{n} \to 4. Both sides agree on the limiting slope 4.

subsection.title: End-of-chapter hook
subsection.p: A limit watches a quantity approach a target. The next chapter chooses one specific limit: the quotient of change in output over change in input as h\to 0:
This limit—when it exists—is the instantaneous rate of change: the derivative.
